9	/-!
10	# Degree slices of the relative-divisor functor + the degree-refined Abel map
11	
12	Campaign milestones **D1'** (degree-`d` divisor functor `DivFunctorDeg`, clopen
13	degree decomposition, base-change stability of the fibre degree) and **A2**
14	(degree-refined Abel map `abelDeg`) of the `instHasPicScheme` campaign
15	(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), on top of the landed divisor
16	functor `Scheme.DivFunctor` (Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §3 Def. `df:div`;
17	`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`).
18	
19	## The fibre degree
20	
21	For a family of relative effective divisors `x : DivFamily π T` (the quotient
22	encoding: `q : O_{X_T} ↠ F = O_D` with invertible kernel ideal `I_D = ker q`),
23	the **fibre degree** at `t : T` is
24	
25	  `x.fiberDeg t := dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t}) = dim_{κ(t)} Γ((X_T)_t, F_t)`,
26	
27	Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`'s degree of the fibre divisor `D_t ⊆ X_t` — the
28	`H⁰`-only, cohomology-free rank.
29	
30	**AUDIT (encoding choice, D1').** The campaign phrase "rank-`d` of the
31	finite-flat pushforward of `O_D`" is realized by its *pointwise shadow*: the
32	in-tree substrate has no `q_* O_D`-as-locally-free-object (that is exactly the
33	B3 rigid-pushforward engine, unbuilt), and for a finite flat family the rank of
34	the pushforward at `t` *equals* `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t})` (pushforward along
35	an affine morphism is exact and commutes with base change).  The fibre-section
36	form is honest at full generality (any `π`, any `T`; `Module.finrank` junk
37	value `0` if the fibre sections are infinite-dimensional, which does not occur
38	for divisor fibres in the relative-curve regime) and is what Kleiman's
39	`deg D_t` means.  When B3 lands, `q_* O_D` is locally free of rank
40	`fiberDeg` and the two vocabularies fuse.
41	
42	**AUDIT (base change, D1').** `fiberDeg` is stable under arbitrary base change
43	`ψ : T' ⟶ T` (`fiberDeg_pullbackAlong`): the fibre of `X_{T'}/T'` at `t'` is
44	the base change of the fibre of `X_T/T` at `t = ψ(t')` along the residue
45	extension `κ(t) → κ(t')`, and `H⁰` of a finitely presented module with proper
46	support commutes with base field extension (Stacks 02KH at `i = 0`).  This is
47	proved **axiom-clean** from the twist-free Γ-fibre core
48	`Scheme.finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport`
49	(`Picard/SchematicSupport.lean`) — NOT from the twisted engine
50	`Scheme.hilbertFunction_quotBaseMap` (`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean`), which
51	still rests on the sorried tensor–pullback leaf
52	`Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso`.  At `m = 0` no twist is needed, so the
53	degree lane stays sorry-free (recon correction to the campaign plan's
54	"the 02KE/02KH engine is landed" — only its untwisted core is).
55	
56	## The clopen degree decomposition — honest form
57	
58	**AUDIT (coproduct pin, D1').** The naive presheaf-level statement
59	"`DivFunctor = ⨿_d DivFunctorDeg d`" is FALSE: on a disconnected `T` a family
60	with non-constant fibre degree lies in no degree piece, and at `T = ∅` every
61	piece contains the (unique) empty family, so the pieces are not disjoint.  The
62	honest pins delivered here are:
63	
64	* every `T`-point decomposes `T` into clopen constant-degree pieces
65	  (`DivFamily.degLocus`, `DivFamily.hasFiberDeg_pullbackAlong_degLocusHom`,
66	  `DivFamily.iSup_degLocus`, `DivFamily.degLocus_disjoint`) — this is the form
67	  the coproduct assembly `G4` (`hom_sigma_decompose`) consumes;
68	* on a nonempty preconnected `T` the canonical comparison
69	  `Σ_d (DivFunctorDeg π d)(T) → DivFunctor π (T)` is a bijection
70	  (`divFunctorDeg_sigma_bijective`);
71	* degree pieces of a common class agree (`DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.unique`,
72	  nonempty `T`).
73	
74	The only non-formal input is **Zariski-local constancy of the fibre degree**.
75	This is TRUE in the campaign regime (relative curve: `D → T` is
76	proper + quasi-finite, hence finite, and a finitely presented `T`-flat module
77	with finite support has finite locally free pushforward — Mumford, *Abelian
78	Varieties* II §5; Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`) but is NOT derivable from the
79	current in-tree substrate (it needs the finite/rank half of the B3 pushforward
80	engine plus `D_t` finite from relative dimension 1).  Following the house gate
81	pattern (`HasPicScheme`), it is pinned as the instance-free Prop-class
82	`HasLocallyConstantDivDeg C` at the AJC curve regime, and every decomposition
83	statement is ALSO provided in hypothesis-parametrized form (an explicit
84	`IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg` argument), so the eventual discharge is a
85	one-line instance.  We deliberately do NOT state the gate for general `π`:
86	for relative dimension `≥ 2` the fibre rank of `O_{D_t}` can jump (only `χ` is
87	locally constant), which is why Kleiman filters `Div` by Hilbert polynomials in
88	general and by the degree only over curves.
89	
90	## The degree ledger and the Abel-map sign (A2)
91	
92	**Sign convention (audit item 7-half).** The Abel map is
93	`abelMapWitness C = abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, i.e.
94	
95	  `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[ker q]`  —
96	
97	a divisor family maps to the *negative* of the class of its ideal sheaf
98	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:461`).  The degree-refined Abel map
99	`abelDeg C d : divFunctorDeg C d ⟶ picSharp C` is the restriction of
100	`abelMapWitness` along the degree-`d` inclusion; its defining property is
101	`abelDeg_app_mk`.  It deliberately lands in `picSharp C` — carving out
102	`picSharpDeg C d` is milestone B4, not this file.
103	
104	**AUDIT (degree-coherence vocabulary, A2).** "The ideal sheaf `ker q` of a
105	rank-`d` family has fibre degree `−d`" is stated in the **rank (colength)
106	vocabulary** — the strongest honestly-provable form today: the χ-ledger
107	(`deg = χ(I) − χ(O)`, campaign P3) is unbuilt, and the adelic
108	`RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor` degree cannot yet be attached to the sheaf-theoretic
109	line bundle `ker q` on a family fibre (that needs the `M ≅ O(div s)`
110	regular-section bricks, also P3).  What IS proved, per fibre `t`:
111	
112	* the ideal restricts to the fibre: the kernel–pullback comparison
113	  `(I_D)_t ≅ ker(q_t)` is an isomorphism (`DivFamily.fiberKernelIso`) and the
114	  fibre ideal inclusion `(I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t}` stays monic
115	  (`DivFamily.mono_fiber_kernel_ι`) with `(I_D)_t` invertible
116	  (`DivFamily.isLocallyTrivial_fiber_kernel`) — `D_t ⊆ X_t` is an honest
117	  effective Cartier divisor (Kleiman §3, note after Def. `df:div`);
118	* its colength is the degree: `O_{X_t}/(I_D)_t ≅ (O_D)_t`
119	  (`DivFamily.fiberCokernelIso`), so
120	  `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(coker((I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t})) = fiberDeg x t = d`
121	  (`DivFamily.fiberDeg_eq_finrank_fiber_cokernel`,
122	  `DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.finrank_fiber_cokernel`).
123	
124	In χ-ledger terms this is exactly `deg_t(ker q) = χ(I_t) − χ(O_{X_t}) = −d`;
125	the translation becomes a theorem once P3 lands.
126	
127	## References
128	
129	Blueprint: to be attached to the campaign's D1'/A2 nodes.
130	Source: [Kleiman], "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §3
131	(Def. `df:div`, Def. `dfn:Abel`, Ex. `ex:DivC`); Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*,
132	II §5 (finite flat pushforward, for the gate's discharge route);
133	Stacks 02KH (`i = 0`) for the base-change core.
134	-/

151	/-- **Transport of the fibre-section dimension along an isomorphism of fibre
152	modules.**  An isomorphism of sheaves of modules on the scheme-theoretic fibre
153	`π₀.fiber s` induces a `κ(s)`-linear equivalence on global sections
154	(evaluation at `⊤` is functorial, and the `κ(s)`-scalar action factors through
155	`Scheme.Hom.fiberResidueMap`), so the `κ(s)`-dimensions agree.  Twist-free
156	sibling of `Scheme.hilbertFunction_eq_finrank_of_iso`
157	(`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean`), serving the degree lane where no tensor
158	operations may enter. -/
159	lemma finrank_fiberSections_eq_of_iso {W B : Scheme.{u}} (π₀ : W ⟶ B) (s : B)
160	    {G G' : (π₀.fiber s).Modules} (e : G ≅ G') :
161	    (letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G
162	     Module.finrank (B.residueField s) Γ(G, ⊤))
163	      = (letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G'
164	         Module.finrank (B.residueField s) Γ(G', ⊤)) := by
165	  letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G
166	  letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G'
167	  have γe := ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules (π₀.fiber s) ⋙
168	    PresheafOfModules.evaluation (π₀.fiber s).ringCatSheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)).mapIso
169	      e).toLinearEquiv
170	  exact LinearEquiv.finrank_eq
171	    { toFun := γe
172	      map_add' := γe.map_add
173	      map_smul' := fun c x => γe.map_smul ((π₀.fiberResidueMap s).hom c) x
174	      invFun := γe.symm
175	      left_inv := γe.left_inv
176	      right_inv := γe.right_inv }

178	/-! ## §1. The fibre degree of a family of relative effective divisors -/

184	/-- The **fibre degree** of a family of relative effective divisors
185	`x : DivFamily π T` at a point `t : T` (Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`):
186	
187	  `deg D_t := dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t}) = dim_{κ(t)} Γ((X_T)_t, F_t)`,
188	
189	the `κ(t)`-dimension of the global sections of the restriction of the divisor
190	structure sheaf `F = O_D` to the scheme-theoretic fibre `(X_T)_t`.  This is
191	the pointwise shadow of "rank of the finite-flat pushforward `q_* O_D`" (equal
192	to it whenever the pushforward exists as a locally free module, i.e. in the
193	relative-curve regime once the B3 engine lands; see the module docstring
194	audit).  `Module.finrank` junk value `0` in the infinite-dimensional case. -/
195	noncomputable def fiberDeg {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
196	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) : ℕ :=
197	  letI := (pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberSectionsModule t
198	    ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t x.F)
199	  Module.finrank (T.left.residueField t)
200	    Γ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t x.F, ⊤)
201	
202	/-- **The fibre degree is well defined on divisor classes**: equivalent
203	families (`DivFamily.Rel`, i.e. same divisor `ker q = ker q'`) have equal
204	fibre degrees — the target isomorphism restricts to each fibre and transports
205	the section dimension. -/
206	theorem Rel.fiberDeg_eq {T : Over S} {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y)
207	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) : x.fiberDeg t = y.fiberDeg t := by
208	  obtain ⟨f, -⟩ := h
209	  exact finrank_fiberSections_eq_of_iso (pullback.snd π T.hom) t
210	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).mapIso f)

236	    (x.pullbackAlong ψ).fiberDeg t' = x.fiberDeg (ψ.left.base t') := by

259	/-! ## §2. The fibre of the ideal sheaf — Cartier fibres and the degree ledger
260	
261	The `[D] ↦ -[ker q]` sign convention of the Abel map (module docstring) is
262	anchored fibrewise: on every fibre `X_t` of the family, the ideal sheaf
263	restricts to an honest invertible ideal `(I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t}` cutting out the
264	fibre divisor `D_t`, and its colength `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(O_{X_t}/(I_D)_t)` is
265	exactly the fibre degree.  In χ-ledger terms (campaign P3, unbuilt):
266	`deg_t(ker q) = χ((I_D)_t) − χ(O_{X_t}) = −deg D_t = −d` for a degree-`d`
267	family. -/
268	
269	/-- **The kernel ideal restricts to an invertible ideal on every fibre**
270	(Kleiman §3, note after Def. `df:div`, specialised to the fibre inclusion):
271	the kernel of the fibre restriction `q_t` of the quotient map is locally
272	trivial of rank one.  Instantiation of the divisor base-change theorem
273	`Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial`
274	(`lem:relative_divisor_base_change`) at Mathlib's fibre square. -/
275	theorem isLocallyTrivial_fiber_kernel {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
276	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
277	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (Limits.kernel
278	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map x.q)) :=
279	  Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial
280	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback (pullback.snd π T.hom)
281	      (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t)) x.q x.epi
282	    (pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (pullback.fst π T.hom)
283	      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) inferInstance)
284	    x.isFinitePresentation x.flat x.kerLocallyTrivial
285	
286	/-- **The ideal inclusion stays monic on every fibre**: `(I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t}`
287	— the fibre divisor `D_t ⊆ X_t` is an effective Cartier divisor (its ideal is
288	an invertible subsheaf, not merely an invertible quotient-kernel).  This is
289	the flat-base-change monomorphism `Modules.mono_pullback_map_kernel_ι`
290	(Stacks 00HL affine-locally) at the fibre square: `T`-flatness of `O_D` is
291	what forbids the ideal from degenerating on special fibres. -/
292	theorem mono_fiber_kernel_ι {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
293	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
294	    Mono ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map
295	      (Limits.kernel.ι x.q)) :=
296	  Modules.mono_pullback_map_kernel_ι
297	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback (pullback.snd π T.hom)
298	      (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t)) x.q x.epi
299	    (pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (pullback.fst π T.hom)
300	      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) inferInstance)
301	    x.isFinitePresentation x.flat x.kerLocallyTrivial
302	
303	/-- **The fibre of the ideal is the ideal of the fibre**: the kernel–pullback
304	comparison `(I_D)_t = (ker q)|_{X_t} ⟶ ker(q_t)` is an isomorphism (Kleiman
305	§3: "Since `D` is `T`-flat, `p^* I` equals the ideal of `D_{T'}`", at
306	`T' = Spec κ(t)`).  The `IsIso` witness is passed to `asIso` explicitly (the
307	project `@asIso` idiom), so no instance search runs. -/
308	noncomputable def fiberKernelIso {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
309	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
310	    (pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t (Limits.kernel x.q)
311	      ≅ Limits.kernel
312	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map x.q) :=
313	  @asIso _ _ _ _
314	    (Modules.pullbackKernelComparison ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t) x.q)
315	    (Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison
316	      (IsPullback.of_hasPullback (pullback.snd π T.hom)
317	        (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t)) x.q x.epi

379	/-- A divisor family **has (constant) fibre degree `d`** when every fibre
380	divisor has degree `d` (Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`).  Vacuously true for every
381	`d` when `T` is empty — which is why the degree pieces of `DivFunctor` are
382	pairwise disjoint only over nonempty bases (`ClassHasFiberDeg.unique`). -/
383	def HasFiberDeg {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
384	  ∀ t : (T.left : Scheme.{u}), x.fiberDeg t = d

387	(`DivFamily.Rel`): well-definedness input for the degree slice of the

389	theorem Rel.hasFiberDeg_iff {T : Over S} {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y)
390	    (d : ℕ) : x.HasFiberDeg d ↔ y.HasFiberDeg d :=
391	  forall_congr' fun t => by rw [h.fiberDeg_eq t]

394	slice `DivFunctorDeg` is a subfunctor, not just a sub-presheaf-of-sets.

396	theorem HasFiberDeg.pullbackAlong {T T' : Over S} {x : DivFamily π T} {d : ℕ}
397	    (hx : x.HasFiberDeg d) (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
398	    (x.pullbackAlong ψ).HasFiberDeg d :=
399	  fun t' => (fiberDeg_pullbackAlong ψ x t').trans (hx (ψ.left.base t'))

402	`Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)` — the carrier predicate of
403	`DivFunctorDeg π d`.  Well defined by `Rel.hasFiberDeg_iff`. -/
404	def ClassHasFiberDeg {T : Over S} (d : ℕ)
405	    (z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)) : Prop :=
406	  Quotient.liftOn z (fun x => x.HasFiberDeg d)
407	    fun _ _ h => propext (h.hasFiberDeg_iff d)

411	    ClassHasFiberDeg d (Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid π T) x) ↔ x.HasFiberDeg d :=
412	  Iff.rfl

415	functoriality input of `DivFunctorDeg`. -/
416	theorem ClassHasFiberDeg.map {T T' : Over S} {d : ℕ}
417	    {z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)} (hz : ClassHasFiberDeg d z)
418	    (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
419	    ClassHasFiberDeg d (Quotient.map (DivFamily.pullbackAlong ψ)
420	      (fun _ _ h => DivFamily.pullbackAlong_rel ψ h) z) := by
421	  induction z using Quotient.ind with
422	  | _ x =>
423	    intro t'
424	    exact (fiberDeg_pullbackAlong ψ x t').trans (hz (ψ.left.base t'))

427	pieces of `DivFunctor` are pairwise disjoint on nonempty `T` (and only there:
428	at `T = ∅` every class has every degree, see the module docstring audit). -/
429	theorem ClassHasFiberDeg.unique {T : Over S}
430	    (hne : Nonempty (T.left : Scheme.{u})) {d d' : ℕ}
431	    {z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)}
432	    (h : ClassHasFiberDeg d z) (h' : ClassHasFiberDeg d' z) : d = d' := by
433	  induction z using Quotient.ind with
434	  | _ x =>
435	    obtain ⟨t⟩ := hne
436	    exact (h t).symm.trans (h' t)

439	docstring audit): a representative of a degree-`d` divisor class has, at
440	every point `t` of `T`, fibre ideal of colength `d`:
441

446	`ker q` of a rank-`d` family has fibre degree `−d`" available before the P3
447	χ-ledger lands. -/

449	    (x : DivFamily π T)

451	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
452	    (letI := (pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberSectionsModule t

454	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map

459	            (Limits.kernel.ι x.q)), ⊤))

469	classes whose every fibre divisor has degree `d`

471	pointwise fibre-section form — see the module docstring audit).  The pullback
472	action is that of `DivFunctor`, restricted along the base-change stability

478	`DivFamily` is automatic, so the `T`-points are honestly Kleiman's degree-`d`

481	    (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1) where
482	  obj T := { z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T.unop) //

489	    ext z
490	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun f => ((TypeCat.Hom.hom f : TypeCat.Fun _ _) : _ → _))
491	      ((DivFunctor π).map_id T)) z.1
492	  map_comp {T T' T''} g h := by
493	    ext z
494	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun f => ((TypeCat.Hom.hom f : TypeCat.Fun _ _) : _ → _))
495	      ((DivFunctor π).map_comp g h)) z.1

614	curve `C/k` and any `T`, a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` is finite

667	`abelMapWitness C`, so on points

669	  `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[ker q]`  (defining property `abelDeg_app_mk`).

671	Sign convention (audit item 7-half): the divisor class maps to the **negative**

679	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] (d : ℕ) :

684	Def. `dfn:Abel`): on the class of a degree-`d` divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` it
685	returns `[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹]`, the additive inverse of the class of the ideal
686	sheaf `I_D = ker q` — the `[D] ↦ -[ker q]` sign convention, verbatim
687	compatible with `abelMap_app_mk` through the inclusion. -/
688	theorem abelDeg_app_mk (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
689	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] (d : ℕ)
690	    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (x : DivFamily C.hom T.unop)

695	        (⟨kernel x.q, x.kerLocallyTrivial⟩ :

11	/-!
12	# Base change of Γ-fibres over a residue field extension, via the schematic support
13	
14	This file supplies the algebra and the schematic-support geometry feeding the Γ-fibre
15	base-change statement `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.gammaFiber_finrank_baseChange_field`
16	(`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean`, blueprint `lem:gamma_fiber_baseChange_field`), which is the
17	flat-base-change core of the fibrewise Hilbert-function invariance
18	(`Scheme.hilbertFunction_quotBaseMap`, Nitsure §1, [Stacks, Tag 02KH] at `i = 0`).
19	
20	On the algebraic side, annihilators only grow under tensoring,
21	`Ann_R M ⊆ Ann_R (M ⊗[R] N)`; a module is finitely generated, finitely presented (over a
22	noetherian base) and faithful over the quotient `R ⧸ Ann_R M` of its base ring by its own
23	annihilator; and a `κ'`-linear equivalence `κ' ⊗[κ] V ≃ₗ[κ'] W` forces
24	`dim_{κ'} W = dim_κ V`.  The last statement holds unconditionally: both sides are
25	`Module.finrank`, and the equivalence identifies the junk value `0` in the
26	infinite-dimensional case as well, so no finiteness case-split is needed.
27	
28	On the geometric side, for a quasi-coherent `F` on a scheme `Y` and an ideal sheaf `I`
29	whose affine sections lie in the annihilators of the section modules of `F`, the unit
30	`F ⟶ i_* i^* F` of the pullback–pushforward adjunction along the closed immersion
31	`i : V(I) ↪ Y` is an isomorphism.  Taking `I = Ann F` realizes `F ≅ i_* N` with
32	`N = i^* F` on the schematic support `Z = V(Ann F)`, with `N` finitely presented whenever
33	`F` is.  Since the annihilator of a tensor product contains that of either factor, the
34	schematic support of `F ⊗ G` sits inside that of `F`, so proper support is inherited by all
35	twists `F ⊗ L^{⊗m}`.
36	
37	The two sides combine in the last theorem: over a cartesian square of a quasi-compact
38	descent to the schematic support, flat base change along a field extension identifies the
39	global sections of `b^* G` with a base change of the global sections of `G`, whence the
40	equality of dimensions.
41	
42	## Main results
43	
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.annihilator_le_annihilator_tensorProduct` — `Ann_R M ⊆ Ann_R (M ⊗[R] N)`.
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_eq_of_baseChange_linearEquiv` — dimension transport along a
46	  base-change linear equivalence.
47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isIso_unit_subschemeι_of_le_annihilator` — the
48	  closed-immersion adjunction unit is an isomorphism over an ideal sheaf contained in the
49	  annihilator.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportDescentIso` — the descent isomorphism
51	  `F ≅ i_* (i^* F)` along the schematic support.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.hasProperSupport_moduleTensorPow` — proper support passes
53	  to the twists `F ⊗ L^{⊗m}`.
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport` — the Γ-fibre
55	  base-change equality of dimensions over a field extension.
56	
57	## References
58	
59	* [Stacks, Tag 02KH], [Stacks, Tag 02KE]
60	* Nitsure, *Construction of Hilbert and Quot schemes*, §1
61	-/

70	
71	/-- **Annihilator monotonicity under tensoring (left factor)**: any scalar that
72	annihilates `M` annihilates `M ⊗[R] N`.  A scalar `a ∈ Ann_R M` kills every
73	elementary tensor via `a • (m ⊗ n) = (a • m) ⊗ n = 0`, hence the whole tensor
74	product by `TensorProduct.induction_on`.
75	
76	This is the sections-level input to the schematic-support monotonicity
77	`schematicSupport (F ⊗ G) ⊆ schematicSupport F` behind the twisted-fibre proper
78	support reduction of `lem:gamma_fiber_baseChange_field`. -/
79	theorem annihilator_le_annihilator_tensorProduct
80	    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M N : Type*}
81	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] :
82	    Module.annihilator R M ≤ Module.annihilator R (M ⊗[R] N) := by
83	  intro a ha
84	  rw [Module.mem_annihilator] at ha ⊢
85	  intro x
86	  induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
87	  | zero => rw [smul_zero]
88	  | tmul m n => rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', ha m, TensorProduct.zero_tmul]
89	  | add x y hx hy => rw [smul_add, hx, hy, add_zero]
90	
91	/-- **Annihilator monotonicity under tensoring (right factor)**: any scalar that
92	annihilates `N` annihilates `M ⊗[R] N`.  Symmetric companion of
93	`annihilator_le_annihilator_tensorProduct`. -/
94	theorem annihilator_le_annihilator_tensorProduct_right
95	    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M N : Type*}
96	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] :
97	    Module.annihilator R N ≤ Module.annihilator R (M ⊗[R] N) := by
98	  intro a ha
99	  rw [Module.mem_annihilator] at ha ⊢
100	  intro x
101	  induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
102	  | zero => rw [smul_zero]
103	  | tmul m n => rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', TensorProduct.smul_tmul, ha n,
104	      TensorProduct.tmul_zero]
105	  | add x y hx hy => rw [smul_add, hx, hy, add_zero]
106	
107	/-- **Dimension transport across a base-change linear equivalence**: a
108	`k'`-linear equivalence between the base change `k' ⊗[k] V` of a `k`-vector space
109	`V` and a `k'`-vector space `W` forces `dim_{k'} W = dim_{k} V`.
110	
111	Over fields the base-change identity `Module.finrank_baseChange`
112	(`finrank_{k'} (k' ⊗[k] V) = finrank_k V`) holds unconditionally, and the
113	equivalence transports finrank (`LinearEquiv.finrank_eq`).  This is the last step
114	of `lem:gamma_fiber_baseChange_field`: flat base change over the residue field
115	extension supplies the equivalence `e`, and the finrank equality
116	follows with **no** finiteness case-split (both sides are `Module.finrank`, whose
117	junk value `0` in the infinite-dimensional case is identified by `e` as well). -/
118	theorem finrank_eq_of_baseChange_linearEquiv
119	    {k k' : Type*} [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
120	    {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
121	    {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module k' W]
122	    (e : (k' ⊗[k] V) ≃ₗ[k'] W) :
123	    Module.finrank k' W = Module.finrank k V := by
124	  rw [← e.finrank_eq, Module.finrank_baseChange]

126	/-! ## The affine-local heart of the support descent
127	
128	On an affine open `U` of the fibre `X_t`, the section module `M = Γ(F, U)` over
129	the coordinate ring `R = Γ(X, U)` carries the *annihilator ideal*
130	`I = Ann_R M`.  By construction `I` kills `M`, so `M` is a module over the
131	quotient `R ⧸ I` (`Module.quotientAnnihilator`), and this is precisely the
132	statement that `F|_U` descends to the closed subscheme `V(I) = Spec (R ⧸ I)`
133	cut out by the annihilator — the schematic support.  The two algebraic facts
134	the descent needs at this affine level are packaged below:
135	
136	* `module_finite_quotientAnnihilator` — the *coherence descent*: the descended
137	  module `M`, viewed over `R ⧸ I`, is still finitely generated.  This is the
138	  affine content of "`N` is finitely presented on `Z`" in the descent
139	  `F ≅ i_* N` (over the residue field `κ(t)` the fibre is Noetherian, so finite
140	  generation is finite presentation).  Assembled from
141	  `Module.quotientAnnihilator` (the `R ⧸ I`-action), the induced scalar tower
142	  `R → R ⧸ I → M` (`Module.IsTorsionBySet.isScalarTower`), and
143	  `Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite` (a finite generating set over `R` is
144	  a finite generating set over the quotient, along which the action factors).
145	
146	* `annihilator_quotientAnnihilator_eq_bot` — the *sharpness* of the schematic
147	  support: over `R ⧸ I` the module `M` is faithful, `Ann_{R⧸I} M = ⊥`.  Any
148	  `q = mk r` killing `M` has `r • m = mk r • m = 0` for all `m`, so `r ∈ I` and
149	  `q = 0`.  Equivalently (`Module.annihilator_eq_bot`) `FaithfulSMul (R ⧸ I) M`:
150	  the closed subscheme `V(I)` is the *smallest* on which `F|_U` lives, i.e.
151	  `V(Ann_R M)` is the honest schematic support and carries no embedded
152	  thickening. -/
153	
154	/-- **Coherence descent to the schematic support (affine heart)**: a finitely
155	generated `R`-module `M` remains finitely generated over the quotient
156	`R ⧸ Ann_R M` by its annihilator (with the canonical `Module.quotientAnnihilator`
157	action).  This is the affine, sections-level content of "the descended module
158	`N` on the schematic support `Z = V(Ann F)` is coherent" in the support descent
159	`F ≅ i_* N`.
160	
161	The `R ⧸ Ann_R M`-action is `Module.quotientAnnihilator`; the scalar tower
162	`R → R ⧸ Ann_R M → M` is `Module.IsTorsionBySet.isScalarTower` at `S := R`
163	(both `R → R` towers being canonical), and
164	`Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite` transports finite generation upward
165	along the tower (a finite `R`-spanning set spans over the quotient, since the
166	`R`-action factors through it). -/
167	theorem module_finite_quotientAnnihilator
168	    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
169	    [Module.Finite R M] :
170	    letI := Module.quotientAnnihilator (R := R) (M := M)
171	    Module.Finite (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) M := by
172	  letI := Module.quotientAnnihilator (R := R) (M := M)
173	  haveI : IsScalarTower R (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) M :=
174	    Module.IsTorsionBySet.isScalarTower (Module.isTorsionBySet_annihilator R M)
175	  exact Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite R (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) M
176	
177	/-- **Sharpness of the schematic support (affine heart)**: over the quotient
178	`R ⧸ Ann_R M` by its own annihilator, the module `M` is *faithful* — its
179	annihilator is trivial.  Any residue class `q = mk r` annihilating `M` has
180	`r • m = q • m = 0` for every `m` (the `Module.quotientAnnihilator` action is
181	`mk r • m = r • m` definitionally), so `r ∈ Ann_R M`, i.e. `q = 0`.
182	
183	Equivalently `FaithfulSMul (R ⧸ Ann_R M) M` (`Module.annihilator_eq_bot`): the
184	closed subscheme `V(Ann_R M)` is the honest schematic support of `F|_U`, carrying
185	no embedded component — exactly what makes the closed immersion `i : Z ↪ X_t` of
186	the descent `F ≅ i_* N` the scheme-theoretic support rather than an arbitrary
187	thickening. -/
188	theorem annihilator_quotientAnnihilator_eq_bot
189	    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
190	    letI := Module.quotientAnnihilator (R := R) (M := M)
191	    Module.annihilator (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) M = ⊥ := by
192	  letI := Module.quotientAnnihilator (R := R) (M := M)
193	  rw [eq_bot_iff]
194	  intro q hq
195	  rw [Module.mem_annihilator] at hq
196	  obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective q
197	  rw [Submodule.mem_bot, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem, Module.mem_annihilator]
198	  intro m
199	  exact hq m

203	`R ⧸ Ann_R M` by its annihilator (`Module.quotientAnnihilator`), is *finitely
204	presented*.

206	This upgrades `module_finite_quotientAnnihilator` (finite generation) to finite
207	presentation: `R ⧸ Ann_R M` is again Noetherian
208	(`Ideal.Quotient.isNoetherianRing`), so a finitely generated module over it is

210	sections-level content of "`N` is finitely presented on `Z = V(Ann F)`" in the
211	support descent `F ≅ i_* N`.  In the Quot consumer the fibre
212	`X_t` is a scheme of finite type over the residue field `κ(t)`, hence locally
213	Noetherian, so the schematic support `Z` is Noetherian and the finitely
214	generated descended module `N` is automatically finitely presented there. -/
215	theorem finitePresentation_quotientAnnihilator
216	    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
217	    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
218	    letI := Module.quotientAnnihilator (R := R) (M := M)
219	    Module.FinitePresentation (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) M := by
220	  letI := Module.quotientAnnihilator (R := R) (M := M)
221	  haveI : IsScalarTower R (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) M :=
222	    Module.IsTorsionBySet.isScalarTower (Module.isTorsionBySet_annihilator R M)
223	  haveI : Module.Finite (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) M :=

225	  exact Module.finitePresentation_of_finite _ _
226	
227	/-- **Faithfulness of the descended module (affine heart), instance form**: over
228	the quotient `R ⧸ Ann_R M` by its own annihilator the module `M` is *faithful*.
229	
230	This is `annihilator_quotientAnnihilator_eq_bot` transported through
231	`Module.annihilator_eq_bot`, packaging the sharpness of the schematic support
232	(no embedded thickening: `V(Ann_R M)` is the honest scheme-theoretic support)
233	as the `FaithfulSMul` scalar-action fact directly consumable by downstream
234	closed-immersion bookkeeping in the descent `F ≅ i_* N`. -/
235	theorem faithfulSMul_quotientAnnihilator
236	    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
237	    letI := Module.quotientAnnihilator (R := R) (M := M)

243	
244	The support descent `F ≅ i_* N` of `lem:gamma_fiber_baseChange_field`
245	realizes a finitely presented sheaf `F` on `Y` as the pushforward `i_* (i^* F)`
246	of its restriction to the schematic-support closed immersion
247	`i : Z = V(Ann F) ↪ Y`.  The comparison is the unit
248	`η : F ⟶ i_* i^* F` of the pullback–pushforward adjunction, proved an
249	isomorphism affine-locally on a basis.

254	gives `I ≤ Ann_R M` for `M := Γ(F, U)`, and this inclusion is *all* the descent
255	isomorphism needs; the reverse inclusion, which would express sharpness of the
256	support, is not proved here.  Under the tilde/pullback section formula the
257	closed-immersion restriction `Γ(i^* F, i⁻¹ U)` is `(R ⧸ I) ⊗_R M`, and the
258	unit `η.app U` is the canonical map `m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m : M → (R ⧸ I) ⊗_R M`.  The two
259	lemmas below package its inverse and bijectivity for `I ≤ Ann_R M`:
260	
261	* `quotTensorEquivOfLeAnnihilator` / `quotTensorEquivOfLeAnnihilator_apply` — the
262	  `R`-linear equivalence `M ≃ₗ[R] (R ⧸ I) ⊗_R M` whose forward map is
263	  `m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m`.  Since `I` kills `M`, `I • ⊤ = ⊥`, so Mathlib's
264	  `TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I : (R ⧸ I) ⊗_R M ≃ₗ M ⧸ I • ⊤`
265	  collapses to `M ⧸ ⊥ ≅ M` (`Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot`);
266	* `bijective_mk_one_of_le_annihilator` — the resulting bijectivity of the honest
267	  unit map `(TensorProduct.mk R (R ⧸ I) M) 1`, in the `Function.Bijective` form
268	  directly consumed by the section-wise iso criterion
269	  (`Modules.isIso_of_isIso_app_of_isBasis`) when globalizing `η` to the scheme
270	  isomorphism `F ≅ i_* i^* F`. -/
271	
272	/-- **The descent isomorphism, affine heart**: for an ideal `I ≤ Ann_R M` the
273	`R`-linear map `m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m : M → (R ⧸ I) ⊗_R M` is an equivalence.
274	
275	`I ≤ Ann_R M` means `I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) = ⊥`, so
276	`TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I : (R ⧸ I) ⊗_R M ≃ₗ M ⧸ (I • ⊤)`
277	identifies the base change with `M ⧸ ⊥`, which is `M`
278	(`Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot`); composing gives `M ≃ₗ[R] (R ⧸ I) ⊗_R M`.
279	
280	This is the affine, sections-level content of the closed-immersion unit
281	`F ⟶ i_* i^* F` being an isomorphism in the support descent `F ≅ i_* N`:
282	on `U = Spec R` the restriction `Γ(i^* F, i⁻¹ U)` is `(R ⧸ I) ⊗_R Γ(F, U)` and the
283	unit is exactly `m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m`.  Only the inclusion `I ≤ Ann_R M`
284	(`annihilator_ideal_le`) is used; the reverse inclusion is *not* needed for the
285	isomorphism, only for identifying `Z` as the honest (minimal) support, and is not
286	proved here. -/
287	noncomputable def quotTensorEquivOfLeAnnihilator
288	    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
289	    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ Module.annihilator R M) :
290	    M ≃ₗ[R] (R ⧸ I) ⊗[R] M :=
291	  have hbot : I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) = ⊥ := by
292	    rw [eq_bot_iff, Submodule.smul_le]
293	    intro r hr n _
294	    rw [Submodule.mem_bot]
295	    exact (Module.mem_annihilator.mp (hI hr)) n
296	  (Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot (I • ⊤) hbot).symm.trans
297	    (TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I).symm
298	
299	/-- The forward map of `quotTensorEquivOfLeAnnihilator` is the canonical unit
300	`m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m` — i.e. it *is* the (sections of the) closed-immersion adjunction
301	unit `F ⟶ i_* i^* F`, the load-bearing identification for globalizing the descent
302	isomorphism `F ≅ i_* N`. -/
303	theorem quotTensorEquivOfLeAnnihilator_apply
304	    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
305	    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ Module.annihilator R M) (m : M) :
306	    quotTensorEquivOfLeAnnihilator I hI m = (1 : R ⧸ I) ⊗ₜ[R] m := by
307	  have hcomp := TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul_symm_comp_mkQ (M := M) I
308	  simp only [quotTensorEquivOfLeAnnihilator, LinearEquiv.trans_apply]
309	  rw [show (Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) _).symm m
310	        = (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)).mkQ m from rfl]
311	  exact congrArg (fun (f : _ →ₗ[R] _) => f m) hcomp
312	
313	/-- **Bijectivity of the closed-immersion unit (affine heart)**: for `I ≤ Ann_R M`
314	the canonical map `(TensorProduct.mk R (R ⧸ I) M) 1 : M → (R ⧸ I) ⊗_R M`,
315	`m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m`, is bijective.
316	
317	This is `quotTensorEquivOfLeAnnihilator` read as a `Function.Bijective`
318	statement about the honest unit map, the form directly consumable by the
319	section-wise isomorphism criterion `Modules.isIso_of_isIso_app_of_isBasis` when
320	upgrading the closed-immersion adjunction unit `F ⟶ i_* i^* F` to the scheme
321	isomorphism `F ≅ i_* N` of `lem:gamma_fiber_baseChange_field`. -/
322	theorem bijective_mk_one_of_le_annihilator
323	    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
324	    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ Module.annihilator R M) :
325	    Function.Bijective ((TensorProduct.mk R (R ⧸ I) M) 1) := by
326	  have hfun : ((TensorProduct.mk R (R ⧸ I) M) 1) =
327	      (quotTensorEquivOfLeAnnihilator I hI : M → (R ⧸ I) ⊗[R] M) := by
328	    funext m
329	    exact (quotTensorEquivOfLeAnnihilator_apply I hI m).symm
330	  rw [hfun]
331	  exact (quotTensorEquivOfLeAnnihilator I hI).bijective
332	
333	/-- **Bijectivity of the closed-immersion unit, quotient-model-free form**: for
334	an `A`-algebra `B` whose structure map `algebraMap A B` is *surjective* with
335	kernel contained in `Ann_A M`, the canonical map
336	`(TensorProduct.mk A B M) 1 : M → B ⊗_A M`, `m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m`, is bijective.
337	
338	This generalizes `bijective_mk_one_of_le_annihilator` from the literal quotient
339	`B = A ⧸ I` to any surjective presentation of `B`: the first isomorphism theorem
340	(`Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective`) identifies `B ≅ A ⧸ ker` as
341	`A`-algebras, the identification transports the tensor factor
342	(`TensorProduct.congr`) carrying `1 ⊗ₜ m` to `1 ⊗ₜ m`, and the quotient case
343	applies.  It is the exact form consumed by the schematic-support descent: on an
344	affine `U ⊆ Y` the coordinate ring of a closed subscheme `V(I)` is presented by
345	the *surjection* `Γ(Y, U) → Γ(V(I), i⁻¹U)` with kernel `I(U)`
346	(`Scheme.IdealSheafData.subschemeι_app_surjective` / `ker_subschemeι_app`), not
347	as a literal quotient ring. -/
348	theorem bijective_mk_one_of_surjective_of_ker_le_annihilator
349	    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
350	    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
351	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A B))
352	    (hker : RingHom.ker (algebraMap A B) ≤ Module.annihilator A M) :
353	    Function.Bijective ((TensorProduct.mk A B M) 1) := by
354	  classical
355	  set f : A →ₐ[A] B := Algebra.ofId A B with hfdef
356	  have hf : Function.Surjective f := fun b => by
357	    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hsurj b
358	    exact ⟨a, by simpa [hfdef, Algebra.ofId_apply] using ha⟩
359	  let e : (A ⧸ RingHom.ker f.toRingHom) ≃ₐ[A] B :=
360	    Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf
361	  -- `ker (Algebra.ofId A B) = ker (algebraMap A B)` definitionally
362	  have hquot : Function.Bijective
363	      ((TensorProduct.mk A (A ⧸ RingHom.ker f.toRingHom) M) 1) :=
364	    bijective_mk_one_of_le_annihilator (RingHom.ker f.toRingHom) hker
365	  -- transport along `TensorProduct.congr e.toLinearEquiv (refl)`
366	  let t : ((A ⧸ RingHom.ker f.toRingHom) ⊗[A] M) ≃ₗ[A] (B ⊗[A] M) :=
367	    TensorProduct.congr e.toLinearEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl A M)
368	  have hcomp : ∀ m : M, (TensorProduct.mk A B M) 1 m
369	      = t ((TensorProduct.mk A (A ⧸ RingHom.ker f.toRingHom) M) 1 m) := by
370	    intro m
371	    change (1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] m = t ((1 : A ⧸ RingHom.ker f.toRingHom) ⊗ₜ[A] m)
372	    rw [show t ((1 : A ⧸ RingHom.ker f.toRingHom) ⊗ₜ[A] m)
373	        = e.toLinearEquiv 1 ⊗ₜ[A] m from TensorProduct.congr_tmul _ _ _ _]
374	    rw [show e.toLinearEquiv (1 : A ⧸ RingHom.ker f.toRingHom) = 1 from map_one e]
375	  rw [show ⇑((TensorProduct.mk A B M) 1)
376	      = ⇑t ∘ ⇑((TensorProduct.mk A (A ⧸ RingHom.ker f.toRingHom) M) 1)
377	    from funext hcomp]
378	  exact t.bijective.comp hquot

380	/-! ## The scheme-level descent isomorphism `F ≅ i_* i^* F`
381	
382	The global assembly of the affine hearts above: for a quasi-coherent sheaf of
383	modules `F` on a scheme `Y` and an ideal sheaf `I` whose affine sections are
384	contained in the annihilators of the section modules of `F`, the adjunction
385	unit `F ⟶ i_* i^* F` along the closed immersion `i : V(I) ↪ Y` is an
386	isomorphism.
387	
388	The proof is affine-local (`Modules.isIso_iff_isIso_app_affineOpens`): on an
389	affine `U ⊆ Y` the preimage `i⁻¹U` is affine (closed immersions are affine
390	morphisms), the quasi-coherent section formula
391	`pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_sectionLinearEquiv` identifies
392	`Γ(i^* F, i⁻¹U) ≅ Γ(V(I), i⁻¹U) ⊗_{Γ(Y,U)} Γ(F, U)` carrying `1 ⊗ x` to the
393	adjunction-unit image of `x`, and the unit section map becomes exactly
394	`m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m`, bijective by `bijective_mk_one_of_surjective_of_ker_le_annihilator`
395	(the coordinate ring of `V(I)` is the surjective image of `Γ(Y, U)` with kernel
396	`I(U) ⊆ Ann Γ(F, U)`, Mathlib's `subschemeι_app_surjective` +
397	`ker_subschemeι_app`). -/
398	
399	namespace Scheme.Modules
400	
401	open AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
402	
403	/-- **The closed-immersion adjunction unit is an isomorphism over the
404	annihilator** (the support descent of `lem:gamma_fiber_baseChange_field`,
405	general ideal-sheaf form): for a quasi-coherent `F` on `Y` and an ideal sheaf
406	`I` with `I(U) ⊆ Ann_{Γ(Y,U)} Γ(F, U)` for every affine open `U`, the unit
407	`F ⟶ i_* i^* F` of the pullback–pushforward adjunction along the closed
408	immersion `i = I.subschemeι : V(I) ↪ Y` is an isomorphism.  At the annihilator
409	ideal sheaf only the `ofIdeals` inclusion `I(U) ⊆ Ann Γ(F, U)` is used. -/
410	theorem isIso_unit_subschemeι_of_le_annihilator
411	    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (I : Y.IdealSheafData) (F : Y.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
412	    (hI : ∀ U : Y.affineOpens, I.ideal U ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(Y, U.1) Γ(F, U.1)) :
413	    IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction I.subschemeι).unit.app F) := by
414	  refine (Modules.isIso_iff_isIso_app_affineOpens _).mpr fun U => ?_
415	  -- the affine pair `(U ⊆ Y, i⁻¹U ⊆ V(I))` of the closed immersion
416	  have hW : IsAffineOpen (I.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) := U.2.preimage I.subschemeι
417	  letI algInst : Algebra Γ(Y, U.1) Γ(I.subscheme, I.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) :=
418	    (I.subschemeι.appLE U.1 (I.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) le_rfl).hom.toAlgebra
419	  letI modInst : Module Γ(Y, U.1)
420	      Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback I.subschemeι).obj F, I.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) :=
421	    Module.compHom _ (I.subschemeι.appLE U.1 (I.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) le_rfl).hom
422	  -- the quasi-coherent affine section formula for the pullback
423	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ :=
424	    (pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_sectionLinearEquiv I.subschemeι F hW U.2 le_rfl).some
425	  -- the base map at `e = le_rfl` *is* the unit section map
426	  have hbase : ∀ x : Γ(F, U.1),
427	      pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap I.subschemeι F le_rfl x
428	        = (((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction I.subschemeι).unit.app F).app
429	            U.1).hom x := by
430	    intro x
431	    change ((((Scheme.Modules.pullback I.subschemeι).obj F).presheaf.map
432	        (homOfLE le_rfl).op).hom)
433	        ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction I.subschemeι).unit.app F).val.app
434	          (Opposite.op U.1)).hom x) = _
435	    rw [show (homOfLE (le_refl (I.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ U.1))) = 𝟙 (I.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) from rfl,
436	      op_id, CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id]
437	    rfl
438	  -- the algebra heart: `algebraMap = i.app U` is surjective with kernel `I(U)`
439	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective
440	      (algebraMap Γ(Y, U.1) Γ(I.subscheme, I.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)) := by
441	    change Function.Surjective (I.subschemeι.appLE U.1 (I.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) le_rfl).hom
442	    rw [Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app]
443	    exact I.subschemeι_app_surjective U
444	  have hkerle : RingHom.ker (algebraMap Γ(Y, U.1) Γ(I.subscheme, I.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ U.1))
445	      ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(Y, U.1) Γ(F, U.1) := by
446	    change RingHom.ker (I.subschemeι.appLE U.1 (I.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) le_rfl).hom ≤ _
447	    rw [Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app, IdealSheafData.ker_subschemeι_app]
448	    exact hI U
449	  -- assemble: the unit section map is `f ∘ (m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m)`
450	  have hcomp : ⇑((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction I.subschemeι).unit.app
451	        F).app U.1).hom)
452	      = ⇑f ∘ ⇑((TensorProduct.mk Γ(Y, U.1)
453	          Γ(I.subscheme, I.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) Γ(F, U.1)) 1) := by
454	    funext x
455	    exact ((hf x).trans (hbase x)).symm
456	  have hbij : Function.Bijective
457	      ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction I.subschemeι).unit.app F).app
458	        U.1).hom) := by
459	    rw [hcomp]
460	    exact f.bijective.comp
461	      (bijective_mk_one_of_surjective_of_ker_le_annihilator hsurj hkerle)
462	  exact (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective _).mpr hbij
463	
464	/-- **The schematic-support descent: the unit `F ⟶ i_* i^* F` is an
465	isomorphism** at the annihilator ideal sheaf (the geometric half of the descent
466	`F ≅ i_* N` of `lem:gamma_fiber_baseChange_field`): for a quasi-coherent `F`
467	on `Y` with schematic-support immersion
468	`i = schematicSupportι F : V(Ann F) ↪ Y`, the adjunction unit is invertible.
469	Instantiation of `isIso_unit_subschemeι_of_le_annihilator` along the `ofIdeals`
470	inclusion `annihilator_ideal_le`. -/
471	theorem isIso_unit_schematicSupportι
472	    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (F : Y.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
473	    IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
474	      (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι F)).unit.app F) :=
475	  isIso_unit_subschemeι_of_le_annihilator (Scheme.Modules.annihilator F) F
476	    (fun U => Scheme.Modules.annihilator_ideal_le F U)
477	
478	/-- **The support-descent isomorphism `F ≅ i_* N`** with `N := i^* F` on the
479	schematic support `Z = V(Ann F)` (`lem:gamma_fiber_baseChange_field`):
480	packaging of `isIso_unit_schematicSupportι` as an `Iso`, the comparison being
481	the adjunction unit itself. -/
482	noncomputable def schematicSupportDescentIso
483	    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (F : Y.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
484	    F ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι F)).obj
485	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι F)).obj F) :=
486	  @asIso _ _ _ _ _ (isIso_unit_schematicSupportι F)
487	
488	/-- **The descended module `N = i^* F` is finitely presented on the schematic

494	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι F)).obj

496	  Scheme.Modules.pullback_isFinitePresentation _ F hfp

500	/-! ## Support monotonicity under the sheaf tensor product
501	
502	The twist `F ⊗ L^{⊗m}` (`Scheme.Modules.moduleTensorPow`) has schematic support
503	contained in that of `F` — step (3) of the `lem:gamma_fiber_baseChange_field`
504	reduction.  On an affine `U`, any scalar `r` in the annihilator ideal sheaf of
505	the left factor kills every section `x` of the sheafified tensor product: by
506	local surjectivity of the sheafification unit
507	(`CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_toSheafify'` through the
508	`PresheafOfModules` bridge), `x` is locally — on affine basis members `W` — the
509	image of an honest presheaf-tensor element of `Γ(A, W) ⊗_{Γ(X, W)} Γ(B, W)`,
510	which the restricted scalar `r|_W` kills
511	(`annihilator_le_annihilator_tensorProduct`, valid since
512	`r|_W ∈ (annihilator A).ideal W ≤ Ann Γ(A, W)` by the ideal-sheaf restriction
513	compatibility `IdealSheafData.ideal_le_comap_ideal`); separatedness of the sheaf
514	then forces `r • x = 0` globally on `U`.  Consequently
515	`annihilator A ≤ annihilator (A ⊗ B)` (`ofIdeals` Galois property), the
516	schematic support of the twist closed-immerses into that of `A`
517	(`IdealSheafData.inclusion`), and proper support transfers to every twist. -/
518	
519	open TopologicalSpace in
520	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
521	/-- **Annihilator sections kill the sheaf tensor product (affine heart)**: on an
522	affine open `U`, the annihilator ideal sheaf of `A` is contained in the
523	annihilator of the sections of `sheafTensorObj A B`.  Local surjectivity of the
524	sheafification unit reduces this to the presheaf-tensor statement
525	`annihilator_le_annihilator_tensorProduct` on an affine basis, and sheaf
526	separatedness globalizes the vanishing back to `U`. -/
527	theorem ideal_annihilator_le_annihilator_sheafTensorObj
528	    {X : Scheme.{u}} (A B : X.Modules) (U : X.affineOpens) :
529	    (Scheme.Modules.annihilator A).ideal U
530	      ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Scheme.Modules.sheafTensorObj A B, U.1) := by
531	  classical
532	  intro r hr
533	  rw [Module.mem_annihilator]
534	  intro x
535	  -- the sheafification unit of the presheaf tensor is locally surjective
536	  have hsurj : CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective
537	      (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
538	      ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _).map
539	        ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction
540	          (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).unit.app (Scheme.Modules.tensorPresheaf A B))) := by
541	    rw [PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf_map_sheafificationAdjunction_unit_app]
542	    exact ((Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X).W_toSheafify _).isLocallySurjective
543	  -- for every point of `U` there is an affine `W ∋ p`, `W ≤ U`, with
544	  -- `(r • x)|_W = 0`
545	  have key : ∀ p : U.1, ∃ W : X.Opens, ∃ _ : p.1 ∈ W, ∃ hWU : W ≤ U.1,
546	      ((Scheme.Modules.sheafTensorObj A B).val.map (homOfLE hWU).op).hom (r • x) = 0 := by
547	    intro p
548	    obtain ⟨V, g, ⟨t, ht⟩, hpV⟩ := hsurj.imageSieve_mem (U := U.1) x p.1 p.2
549	    -- refine to an affine basis member `W ∋ p` inside `V`
550	    obtain ⟨W, hWaff, hpW, hWV⟩ :=
551	      Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp X.isBasis_affineOpens hpV
552	    have hWU : W ≤ U.1 := hWV.trans g.le
553	    refine ⟨W, hpW, hWU, ?_⟩
554	    -- the restricted scalar `r|_W` annihilates the presheaf tensor over `W`
555	    have hrW : (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hWU).op).hom r
556	        ∈ (Scheme.Modules.annihilator A).ideal ⟨W, hWaff⟩ :=
557	      Scheme.IdealSheafData.ideal_le_comap_ideal (Scheme.Modules.annihilator A)
558	        (U := ⟨W, hWaff⟩) (V := U) hWU hr
559	    have hkill : (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hWU).op).hom r
560	        ∈ Module.annihilator Γ(X, W) (TensorProduct Γ(X, W) Γ(A, W) Γ(B, W)) :=
561	      annihilator_le_annihilator_tensorProduct
562	        (Scheme.Modules.annihilator_ideal_le A ⟨W, hWaff⟩ hrW)
563	    -- restrict the local presheaf-tensor preimage `t` of `x|_V` to `W`
564	    have hnat := Scheme.Modules.tensorSectionHom_naturality_apply A B
565	      (V := W) (W := V) (homOfLE hWV).op t
566	    -- `(r • x)|_W = r|_W • x|_W` (semilinearity of restriction)
567	    have hres : ((Scheme.Modules.sheafTensorObj A B).val.map (homOfLE hWU).op).hom (r • x)
568	        = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hWU).op).hom r
569	            • ((Scheme.Modules.sheafTensorObj A B).val.map (homOfLE hWU).op).hom x :=
570	      PresheafOfModules.map_smul _ _ _ _
571	    rw [hres]
572	    -- `x|_W` is the image of the restricted presheaf tensor `t|_W`:
573	    -- restrict in two steps `U ⊇ V ⊇ W` (`congr_map_apply` + `map_comp_apply`),
574	    -- recognize `x|_V` as the unit image of `t` (`ht`), and pull the last
575	    -- restriction through the unit (`tensorSectionHom` naturality)
576	    have e1 : (Scheme.Modules.sheafTensorObj A B).val.map (homOfLE hWU).op x
577	        = (Scheme.Modules.sheafTensorObj A B).val.map (homOfLE hWV).op
578	            ((Scheme.Modules.sheafTensorObj A B).val.map g.op x) :=

581	          rw [show (homOfLE hWU : W ⟶ U.1) = (homOfLE hWV : W ⟶ V) ≫ g from

594	    rw [hxW]

596	    -- presheaf tensor
597	    have hlin : (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hWU).op).hom r
598	          • Scheme.Modules.tensorSectionHom A B W

602	              • (Scheme.Modules.tensorPresheaf A B).map (homOfLE hWV).op t) :=

604	    rw [hlin, Module.mem_annihilator.mp hkill _, map_zero]

616	/-- **Annihilator monotonicity for the sheaf tensor product, ideal-sheaf form**:
617	`annihilator A ≤ annihilator (A ⊗ B)` (`ofIdeals` Galois property applied to the
618	affine heart `ideal_annihilator_le_annihilator_sheafTensorObj`). -/
619	theorem annihilator_le_annihilator_sheafTensorObj
620	    {X : Scheme.{u}} (A B : X.Modules) :
621	    Scheme.Modules.annihilator A
622	      ≤ Scheme.Modules.annihilator (Scheme.Modules.sheafTensorObj A B) :=
623	  Scheme.IdealSheafData.le_ofIdeals_iff.mpr
624	    (fun U => ideal_annihilator_le_annihilator_sheafTensorObj A B U)

628	/-- **Proper support descends along annihilator inclusions**: if
629	`annihilator A ≤ annihilator C` then the schematic support of `C`
630	closed-immerses into that of `A` (`IdealSheafData.inclusion`), so properness of
631	the support of `A` over `S` transfers to `C` (closed immersions are proper,
632	propers compose). -/
633	theorem HasProperSupport.of_annihilator_le {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
634	    {A C : X.Modules}
635	    (h : Scheme.Modules.annihilator A ≤ Scheme.Modules.annihilator C)
636	    (hA : Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport f A) :
637	    Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport f C := by
638	  haveI : IsProper ((Scheme.Modules.annihilator A).subschemeι ≫ f) := hA
639	  have hfac : Scheme.IdealSheafData.inclusion h
640	        ≫ ((Scheme.Modules.annihilator A).subschemeι ≫ f)
641	      = (Scheme.Modules.annihilator C).subschemeι ≫ f := by
642	    rw [← Category.assoc, Scheme.IdealSheafData.inclusion_subschemeι]
643	  change IsProper ((Scheme.Modules.annihilator C).subschemeι ≫ f)
644	  rw [← hfac]
645	  infer_instance

647	/-- **Proper support transfers to sheaf-tensor twists** (left factor): the
648	schematic support of `A ⊗ B` sits inside that of `A`, so proper support of `A`
649	over `S` gives proper support of the tensor. -/
650	theorem hasProperSupport_sheafTensorObj {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
651	    {A : X.Modules} (B : X.Modules)
652	    (hA : Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport f A) :
653	    Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport f (Scheme.Modules.sheafTensorObj A B) :=
654	  HasProperSupport.of_annihilator_le f
655	    (annihilator_le_annihilator_sheafTensorObj A B) hA

658	(`Scheme.Modules.moduleTensorPow`), step (3) of the
659	`lem:gamma_fiber_baseChange_field` reduction: `moduleTensorPow F L m` is by
660	definition `sheafTensorObj F (tensorPow L m)`. -/
661	theorem hasProperSupport_moduleTensorPow {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
662	    {F : X.Modules} (L : X.Modules) (m : ℕ)
663	    (hF : Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport f F) :
664	    Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport f (Scheme.Modules.moduleTensorPow F L m) :=
665	  hasProperSupport_sheafTensorObj f (Scheme.Modules.tensorPow L m) hF

669	/-! ## The Γ-fibre flat base change over a field, via the schematic support
670	
671	The scheme-level assembly of `lem:gamma_fiber_baseChange_field` for a single
672	quasi-coherent module with proper support: for a cartesian square
673	
674	```
675	Xt' ──b──→ Xt
676	 │f'        │f
677	 ↓          ↓
678	Spec K' ──Spec.map φ──→ Spec K
679	```
680	
681	over fields `K`, `K'` and a quasi-coherent `G` on `Xt` whose schematic support
682	is proper over `K`, the `K'`-dimension of `Γ(Xt', b^* G)` equals the
683	`K`-dimension of `Γ(Xt, G)` (each via the structural `ΓSpecIso`-composite
684	scalar action, the shape of `Scheme.Hom.fiberSectionsModule`).
685	
686	Route: `Xt` is only locally of finite type over `K` — not qcqs — so Stacks
687	02KH cannot be applied on `Xt` itself.  Descend to the schematic support
688	`i : Z = V(Ann G) ↪ Xt` (proper over `K` by hypothesis, hence qcqs):
689	
690	1. `G ≅ i_* N` for `N := i^* G` (`isIso_unit_schematicSupportι`);
691	2. `b^*(i_* N) ≅ j_* (w^* N)` for the base-changed closed immersion
692	   `j : W = Z ×_{Xt} Xt' ↪ Xt'` (`flatBaseChangeCohomology` on the
693	   closed-immersion square — `i` is qcqs, `b` is flat as the base change of
694	   the field extension `Spec.map φ`);
695	3. pushing forward to `Spec K'` and evaluating at `⊤` identifies
696	   `Γ(Xt', b^* G)` with `Γ(Spec K', (j ≫ f')_* (w^* N))`,
697	   `Γ(Spec K', ⊤)`-linearly (`finrank_eq_of_ringEquiv_addEquiv` transports the
698	   dimension along `ΓSpecIso K'`), and similarly on the unprimed side;
699	4. the pasted square `W → Z → Spec K ← Spec K' ← W` is cartesian
700	   (`IsPullback.paste_vert`) with `i ≫ f` proper — qcqs — so the CLOSED
701	   02KE heart `pullback_baseMap_sectionLinearEquiv_of_quasiCompact` at
702	   `V = U = ⊤` yields `Γ(Spec K', ⊤) ⊗ Γ(Z, N) ≃ₗ Γ(W, w^* N)`, and
703	   `finrank_eq_of_baseChange_linearEquiv` (with the field structures
704	   transported along `ΓSpecIso` via `MulEquiv.isField`) closes the count. -/
705	
706	/-- **Dimension transport across a ring isomorphism**: a ring isomorphism
707	`i : R ≃+* R'` together with an additive equivalence `j : M ≃+ M'`
708	intertwining the scalar actions transports `Module.finrank`.  This is the
709	`Cardinal.toNat` image of `rank_eq_of_equiv_equiv`; it is the bookkeeping
710	device carrying `κ'`-dimensions across the `ΓSpecIso` identification
711	`Γ(Spec κ', ⊤) ≃+* κ'` in the Γ-fibre base-change assembly. -/
712	theorem finrank_eq_of_ringEquiv_addEquiv
713	    {R R' : Type*} {M M' : Type v} [Semiring R] [Semiring R']
714	    [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid M'] [Module R M] [Module R' M']
715	    (i : R ≃+* R') (j : M ≃+ M')
716	    (hc : ∀ (r : R) (m : M), j (r • m) = i r • j m) :
717	    Module.finrank R M = Module.finrank R' M' :=
718	  congrArg Cardinal.toNat (rank_eq_of_equiv_equiv i j i.bijective hc)

737	    {K K' : CommRingCat.{u}} (hK : IsField K) (hK' : IsField K')
738	    {Xt Xt' : Scheme.{u}} {f : Xt ⟶ Spec K} {f' : Xt' ⟶ Spec K'}
739	    {b : Xt' ⟶ Xt} {φ : K ⟶ K'}
740	    (sq : IsPullback b f' f (Spec.map φ))
741	    (G : Xt.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent]
742	    (hps : Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport f G) :
743	    (letI := Module.compHom Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback b).obj G, ⊤)
744	        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso K').inv ≫ f'.appTop).hom
745	     Module.finrank K' Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback b).obj G, ⊤))
746	      = (letI := Module.compHom Γ(G, ⊤) ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso K).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom
747	         Module.finrank K Γ(G, ⊤)) := by
748	  letI := Module.compHom Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback b).obj G, ⊤)
749	      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso K').inv ≫ f'.appTop).hom
750	  letI := Module.compHom Γ(G, ⊤) ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso K).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom
751	  -- field structures on the global sections of the two affine bases
752	  letI : Field ↥Γ(Spec K, ⊤) :=
753	    (MulEquiv.isField hK (Scheme.ΓSpecIso K).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.toMulEquiv).toField
754	  letI : Field ↥Γ(Spec K', ⊤) :=
755	    (MulEquiv.isField hK' (Scheme.ΓSpecIso K').commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.toMulEquiv).toField
756	  -- properness of the schematic support over `Spec K`, hence qcqs instances
757	  haveI hproper : IsProper (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G ≫ f) := hps
758	  haveI : QuasiCompact (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G) :=

765	    letI : Field ↥K := hK.toField

772	      G).IsQuasicoherent :=
773	    pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom _ G ‹_›
774	  -- the closed-immersion base-change square and its pasting over `Spec.map φ`

776	      (pullback.snd (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G) b)
777	      (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G) b :=
778	    IsPullback.of_hasPullback _ _
779	  have sqZ : IsPullback (pullback.fst (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G) b)
780	      (pullback.snd (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G) b ≫ f')
781	      (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G ≫ f) (Spec.map φ) :=
782	    sq1.paste_vert sq
783	  -- support descent `G ≅ i_* N` and the flat-base-change exchange
784	  haveI hunit := Scheme.Modules.isIso_unit_schematicSupportι G
785	  obtain ⟨eEx⟩ := flatBaseChangeCohomology sq1
786	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G)).obj G)
787	  -- assembled isos over the two affine bases, and their `⊤`-section equivalences
788	  let EL : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f').obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback b).obj G)
789	      ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
790	            (pullback.snd (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G) b ≫ f')).obj
791	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
792	            (pullback.fst (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G) b)).obj
793	            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G)).obj G)) :=
794	    (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f').mapIso
795	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback b).mapIso
796	          (asIso ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
797	            (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G)).unit.app G)) ≪≫ eEx)
798	      ≪≫ ((Scheme.Modules.pushforwardComp
799	            (pullback.snd (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G) b) f').app
800	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
801	            (pullback.fst (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G) b)).obj
802	            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G)).obj G))).symm
803	  let ER : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj G
804	      ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G ≫ f)).obj
805	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G)).obj G) :=
806	    (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).mapIso
807	        (asIso ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
808	          (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G)).unit.app G))
809	      ≪≫ ((Scheme.Modules.pushforwardComp (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G) f).app
810	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G)).obj G)).symm
811	  let γL := ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules (Spec K') ⋙
812	      PresheafOfModules.evaluation (Spec K').ringCatSheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)).mapIso
813	        EL).toLinearEquiv
814	  let γR := ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules (Spec K) ⋙
815	      PresheafOfModules.evaluation (Spec K).ringCatSheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)).mapIso
816	        ER).toLinearEquiv

819	      = Module.finrank ↥Γ(Spec K', ⊤)
820	          Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
821	              (pullback.snd (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G) b ≫ f')).obj
822	            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
823	              (pullback.fst (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G) b)).obj
824	              ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι G)).obj G)), ⊤) :=
825	    finrank_eq_of_ringEquiv_addEquiv
826	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso K').symm.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv

10	/-!
11	# Universal property of the flat-locus stratification (Nitsure §4, `n = 0`)
12	
13	This file proves the *representability* layer of the flat-locus
14	stratification and assembles it into the universal theorem
15	`AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal` (sorry-free): a
16	morphism `q : T ⟶ X` whose pulled-back module is flat of constant fiber
17	rank `e` factors uniquely through the rank-`e` stratum
18	`stratumι : stratum G e hcov ⟶ X` of
19	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EntryIdealStratum`, the stratum itself carries a
20	flat pullback, and over a noetherian base the finitely many rank strata
21	form the universal flattening stratification — parts (i)+(ii) of the
22	special case `n = 0` of the flattening-stratification theorem in
23	[Nitsure §4].
24	
25	## Contents
26	
27	* §1 — bridges: matrix presentations of pullback section modules
28	  (`exists_matrixPresentation_pullback_sections`, via the Lane F section
29	  formula `pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_sectionLinearEquiv`), transport of
30	  flatness between the natural and the `appLE`-restriction module structures
31	  (`flat_compHom_congr`), and extraction of section flatness from
32	  `CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T)` (`flat_sections_of_coherentSheafFlat_id`,
33	  `coherentSheafFlat_id_of_charts`).
34	* §2 — the rank dictionary: `rankAtStalk` of an affine section module
35	  computes the `pointRank` (`rankAtStalk_sections_eq_pointRank`), and the
36	  point rank of a pullback module is the point rank at the image point
37	  (`pointRank_pullback`; no flatness hypotheses, via
38	  `Ideal.fiberRank_baseChange`).
39	* §3 — Stage D1: the kernel bound `strataData_le_ker` (a flat
40	  constant-rank-`e` pullback kills the strata ideal) and the unique
41	  factorization `existsUnique_stratumLift` through the closed immersion
42	  `stratumι` (`IsClosedImmersion.lift`).
43	* §4 — Stage D2: the stratum pullback is flat over the stratum
44	  (`coherentSheafFlat_stratum`): on chart preimages the section module is
45	  presented with vanishing relation matrix, hence free.
46	* §5 — chart supply on a locally noetherian base
47	  (`exists_presentationChart_mem`, via the Nakayama prolongation) and the
48	  chart locus `chartLocus` with its rank bounds.
49	* §6 — the rank stratum `rankStratum`/`rankStratumι` over the chart locus:
50	  a locally closed immersion with support exactly the rank-`e` locus
51	  (`mem_range_rankStratumι_iff`) and flat pullback
52	  (`coherentSheafFlat_rankStratum`); flatness is stable under arbitrary
53	  pullback (`coherentSheafFlat_id_pullback`).
54	* §7 — the rank bound on a noetherian base (`exists_pointRank_le`) and
55	  openness of the rank fibers of a flat pullback
56	  (`isOpen_pointRank_pullback_eq`).
57	* §8 — unique factorization of a constant-rank flat morphism through the
58	  rank stratum (`existsUnique_factor_rankStratum`).
59	* §9 — the universal theorem `flatLocusStratification_universal`.
60

62	§`sec:flatstrat_universal`.

64	special case `n = 0` (`references/nitsure-hilbert-quot-src/`

66	-/

486	
487	These declarations build the annihilator ideal sheaf of a sheaf of modules and the
488	support/properness predicates of `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`,
489	§"Support and freeness predicates". Mathlib (at the pinned commit) carries no
490	annihilator ideal sheaf for sheaves of modules on a scheme, nor a schematic-support
491	or proper-support predicate, so they are built here.
492	
493	The annihilator is packaged via `Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdeals`, exactly mirroring
494	Mathlib's `Scheme.Hom.ker` (which is `ofIdeals fun U ↦ RingHom.ker (f.app U).hom`):
495	`ofIdeals` produces *the largest ideal sheaf contained in* an arbitrary affine-local
496	family of ideals, so the structure's `map_ideal_basicOpen` coherence is discharged
497	internally and need not be supplied at definition time. The basic-open coherence that
498	makes the local annihilators agree with `ofIdeals` (the analogue of `Hom.ker_apply`,
499	`def:modules_annihilator`) is the separate characterization lemma `annihilator_ideal`,
500	which depends on the not-yet-closed QCoh→localization bridge
501	`isLocalizedModule_basicOpen` (`lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen`) together with
502	the algebra engine `Module.annihilator_isLocalizedModule_eq_map`

514	`Ann_{Γ(X,U)}(Γ(F,U))` of the `Γ(X,U)`-module of sections `Γ(F,U)`. The ideal sheaf
515	is assembled with `Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdeals`, the largest ideal sheaf contained
516	in that affine-local family — exactly the construction used for `Scheme.Hom.ker`. This
517	sidesteps proving the basic-open coherence (`map_ideal_basicOpen`) at definition time;
518	the identity `(annihilator F).ideal U = Ann_{Γ(X,U)}(Γ(F,U))` is the downstream
519	characterization lemma (`annihilator_ideal`, blocked on the QCoh localization bridge).

521	This is a project-local primitive: Mathlib does not carry an annihilator ideal sheaf
522	for sheaves of modules on a scheme. -/
523	noncomputable def annihilator (F : X.Modules) : X.IdealSheafData :=

10	/-!
11	# Universal property of the flat-locus stratification (Nitsure §4, `n = 0`)
12	
13	This file proves the *representability* layer of the flat-locus
14	stratification and assembles it into the universal theorem
15	`AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal` (sorry-free): a
16	morphism `q : T ⟶ X` whose pulled-back module is flat of constant fiber
17	rank `e` factors uniquely through the rank-`e` stratum
18	`stratumι : stratum G e hcov ⟶ X` of
19	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EntryIdealStratum`, the stratum itself carries a
20	flat pullback, and over a noetherian base the finitely many rank strata
21	form the universal flattening stratification — parts (i)+(ii) of the
22	special case `n = 0` of the flattening-stratification theorem in
23	[Nitsure §4].
24	
25	## Contents
26	
27	* §1 — bridges: matrix presentations of pullback section modules
28	  (`exists_matrixPresentation_pullback_sections`, via the Lane F section
29	  formula `pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_sectionLinearEquiv`), transport of
30	  flatness between the natural and the `appLE`-restriction module structures
31	  (`flat_compHom_congr`), and extraction of section flatness from
32	  `CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T)` (`flat_sections_of_coherentSheafFlat_id`,
33	  `coherentSheafFlat_id_of_charts`).
34	* §2 — the rank dictionary: `rankAtStalk` of an affine section module
35	  computes the `pointRank` (`rankAtStalk_sections_eq_pointRank`), and the
36	  point rank of a pullback module is the point rank at the image point
37	  (`pointRank_pullback`; no flatness hypotheses, via
38	  `Ideal.fiberRank_baseChange`).
39	* §3 — Stage D1: the kernel bound `strataData_le_ker` (a flat
40	  constant-rank-`e` pullback kills the strata ideal) and the unique
41	  factorization `existsUnique_stratumLift` through the closed immersion
42	  `stratumι` (`IsClosedImmersion.lift`).
43	* §4 — Stage D2: the stratum pullback is flat over the stratum
44	  (`coherentSheafFlat_stratum`): on chart preimages the section module is
45	  presented with vanishing relation matrix, hence free.
46	* §5 — chart supply on a locally noetherian base
47	  (`exists_presentationChart_mem`, via the Nakayama prolongation) and the
48	  chart locus `chartLocus` with its rank bounds.
49	* §6 — the rank stratum `rankStratum`/`rankStratumι` over the chart locus:
50	  a locally closed immersion with support exactly the rank-`e` locus
51	  (`mem_range_rankStratumι_iff`) and flat pullback
52	  (`coherentSheafFlat_rankStratum`); flatness is stable under arbitrary
53	  pullback (`coherentSheafFlat_id_pullback`).
54	* §7 — the rank bound on a noetherian base (`exists_pointRank_le`) and
55	  openness of the rank fibers of a flat pullback
56	  (`isOpen_pointRank_pullback_eq`).
57	* §8 — unique factorization of a constant-rank flat morphism through the
58	  rank stratum (`existsUnique_factor_rankStratum`).
59	* §9 — the universal theorem `flatLocusStratification_universal`.
60	
61	Blueprint chapter: `Picard_FlatteningStratification.tex`,
62	§`sec:flatstrat_universal`.
63	Source: [Nitsure], §4, proof of the flattening-stratification theorem,
64	special case `n = 0` (`references/nitsure-hilbert-quot-src/`
65	`nitsure-hilbert-quot.tex`, L1849–L1885).
66	-/

82	variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ X) (G : X.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent]

84	/-- Elementwise fibre-side `appLE` coherence: restricting the image of
85	`appLE` equals `appLE` into the smaller open. -/
86	private lemma appLE_res_apply' {W W' : Y.Opens} {V : X.Opens}
87	    (e : W ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ V) (h : W' ≤ W) (u : Γ(X, V)) :
88	    (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom ((g.appLE V W e).hom u) =
89	      (g.appLE V W' (h.trans e)).hom u := by
90	  have h1 := congrArg (fun (φ : Γ(X, V) ⟶ Γ(Y, W')) => φ.hom u)
91	    (Scheme.Hom.appLE_map (f := g) e (homOfLE h).op)
92	  simpa only [CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_apply] using h1
93	
94	/-- Elementwise base-side `appLE` coherence: `appLE` of a restricted base
95	section equals `appLE` from the larger base open. -/
96	private lemma appLE_base_res_apply' {V' V : X.Opens} {W : Y.Opens}
97	    (h : V' ≤ V) (e' : W ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ V') (e : W ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ V) (u : Γ(X, V)) :
98	    (g.appLE V' W e').hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom u) =
99	      (g.appLE V W e).hom u := by
100	  have h1 := congrArg (fun (φ : Γ(X, V) ⟶ Γ(Y, W)) => φ.hom u)
101	    (Scheme.Hom.map_appLE (f := g) e' (homOfLE h).op)
102	  simpa only [CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_apply] using h1
103	
104	/-- **Matrix presentations pull back to section modules** (the geometric
105	base-change of a local presentation, [Nitsure §4]: "the pulled-back
106	sequence is exact by right-exactness of tensor products").  For a morphism
107	`g : Y ⟶ X`, an affine `V ⊆ X`, an affine `W ⊆ g⁻¹V` and an `ee`-generator
108	presentation `P` of `Γ(G, V)`, the section module `Γ(g^*G, W)` admits an
109	`ee`-generator presentation whose relation matrix is the image of that of
110	`P` under `g.appLE`. -/
111	theorem exists_matrixPresentation_pullback_sections
112	    {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) {W : Y.Opens} (hW : IsAffineOpen W)
113	    (e : W ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ V) {ee mm : ℕ}
114	    (P : MatrixPresentation Γ(X, V) Γ(G, V) ee mm) :
115	    ∃ P' : MatrixPresentation Γ(Y, W)
116	      Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj G, W) ee mm,
117	      P'.relMatrix = P.relMatrix.map (g.appLE V W e).hom := by
118	  letI : Algebra Γ(X, V) Γ(Y, W) := (g.appLE V W e).hom.toAlgebra
119	  letI : Module Γ(X, V) Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj G, W) :=
120	    Module.compHom _ (g.appLE V W e).hom
121	  obtain ⟨⟨eqv, -⟩⟩ :=
122	    pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_sectionLinearEquiv g G hW hV e
123	  refine ⟨(P.baseChange Γ(Y, W)).congr eqv, ?_⟩
124	  rw [Module.MatrixPresentation.congr_relMatrix,
125	    Module.MatrixPresentation.baseChange_relMatrix,
126	    RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
127	
128	end PullbackPresentation

130	section FlatBridge
131	
132	/-- Transport of `Module.Flat` between the canonical module structure and a
133	`Module.compHom` structure along a pointwise-identity ring endomorphism
134	(the `appLE` of the identity morphism is the identity restriction, but not
135	definitionally the identity ring hom). -/
136	private lemma flat_compHom_congr {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type u}
137	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f : R →+* R) (hf : ∀ r, f r = r) :
138	    (letI : Module R M := Module.compHom M f
139	     Module.Flat R M) ↔ Module.Flat R M := by
140	  have h : (Module.compHom M f : Module R M) = ‹Module R M› :=
141	    Module.ext' _ _ fun r m => by
142	      change f r • m = r • m
143	      rw [hf r]
144	  exact (congrArg (fun i : Module R M => @Module.Flat R M _ _ i) h).to_iff
145	
146	variable {T : Scheme.{u}}
147	
148	/-- The `appLE` of the identity morphism at equal opens is pointwise the
149	identity. -/
150	private lemma id_appLE_apply {W : T.Opens}
151	    (e : W ≤ (𝟙 T : T ⟶ T) ⁻¹ᵁ W) (r : Γ(T, W)) :
152	    ((𝟙 T : T ⟶ T).appLE W W e).hom r = r := by
153	  rw [Scheme.id_appLE]
154	  exact presheaf_map_self (X := T) e r
155	
156	/-- **Extraction of section flatness from flatness over the identity**: if
157	`G` is flat over `T` via `𝟙 T` (the encoding of "the coherent sheaf `G` is
158	flat" in `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat`), then the sections over every affine
159	open form a flat module over the section ring. -/
160	theorem flat_sections_of_coherentSheafFlat_id {G : T.Modules}
161	    (h : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T) G) {W : T.Opens}
162	    (hW : IsAffineOpen W) : Module.Flat Γ(T, W) Γ(G, W) :=
163	  (flat_compHom_congr ((𝟙 T : T ⟶ T).appLE W W (le_refl W)).hom
164	    (id_appLE_apply _)).mp (h hW hW (le_refl W))
165	
166	/-- **Flatness over the identity from an affine cover of flat sections**:
167	if the sections of `G` over each member of an affine open cover of `T` are
168	flat over the respective section rings, then `G` is flat over `T` via
169	`𝟙 T`. -/
170	theorem coherentSheafFlat_id_of_charts (G : T.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent]
171	    {ι : Type u} (Wc : ι → T.Opens) (hWc : ∀ j, IsAffineOpen (Wc j))
172	    (hcover : ∀ y : T, ∃ j, y ∈ Wc j)
173	    (hflat : ∀ j, Module.Flat Γ(T, Wc j) Γ(G, Wc j)) :
174	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T) G := by
175	  intro U hU V hV eV
176	  exact flat_section_of_affine_cover (𝟙 T) G Wc hWc Wc hWc
177	    (fun j => le_refl _) hcover
178	    (fun j => (flat_compHom_congr
179	      ((𝟙 T : T ⟶ T).appLE (Wc j) (Wc j) (le_refl _)).hom
180	      (id_appLE_apply _)).mpr (hflat j)) hU hV eV

485	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — annihilator ideal sheaf and schematic support
486	
487	These declarations build the annihilator ideal sheaf of a sheaf of modules and the
488	support/properness predicates of `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`,
489	§"Support and freeness predicates". Mathlib (at the pinned commit) carries no
490	annihilator ideal sheaf for sheaves of modules on a scheme, nor a schematic-support
491	or proper-support predicate, so they are built here.
492	
493	The annihilator is packaged via `Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdeals`, exactly mirroring
494	Mathlib's `Scheme.Hom.ker` (which is `ofIdeals fun U ↦ RingHom.ker (f.app U).hom`):
495	`ofIdeals` produces *the largest ideal sheaf contained in* an arbitrary affine-local
496	family of ideals, so the structure's `map_ideal_basicOpen` coherence is discharged
497	internally and need not be supplied at definition time. The basic-open coherence that
498	makes the local annihilators agree with `ofIdeals` (the analogue of `Hom.ker_apply`,
499	`def:modules_annihilator`) is the separate characterization lemma `annihilator_ideal`,
500	which depends on the not-yet-closed QCoh→localization bridge
501	`isLocalizedModule_basicOpen` (`lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen`) together with
502	the algebra engine `Module.annihilator_isLocalizedModule_eq_map`
503	(`lem:annihilator_localization_eq_map`); see the handoff in
504	`task_results/.../QuotScheme.md`. -/
505	
506	namespace Scheme.Modules
507	
508	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
509	
510	/-- The **annihilator ideal sheaf** of a sheaf of modules `F` on a scheme `X`
511	(`def:modules_annihilator`).
512	
513	On each affine open `U`, the intended section is the annihilator
514	`Ann_{Γ(X,U)}(Γ(F,U))` of the `Γ(X,U)`-module of sections `Γ(F,U)`. The ideal sheaf
515	is assembled with `Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdeals`, the largest ideal sheaf contained
516	in that affine-local family — exactly the construction used for `Scheme.Hom.ker`. This
517	sidesteps proving the basic-open coherence (`map_ideal_basicOpen`) at definition time;
518	the identity `(annihilator F).ideal U = Ann_{Γ(X,U)}(Γ(F,U))` is the downstream
519	characterization lemma (`annihilator_ideal`, blocked on the QCoh localization bridge).
520	
521	This is a project-local primitive: Mathlib does not carry an annihilator ideal sheaf
522	for sheaves of modules on a scheme. -/
523	noncomputable def annihilator (F : X.Modules) : X.IdealSheafData :=
524	  IdealSheafData.ofIdeals fun U => Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1)
525	
526	/-- The component of the annihilator ideal sheaf at an affine open is contained in the
527	module annihilator of the sections. This is the always-available (`ofIdeals`) direction
528	of the characterization; the reverse inclusion is the basic-open coherence blocked on
529	`isLocalizedModule_basicOpen`. Project-local because `annihilator` is. -/
530	lemma annihilator_ideal_le (F : X.Modules) (U : X.affineOpens) :
531	    (annihilator F).ideal U ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1) :=
532	  IdealSheafData.ideal_ofIdeals_le _ _
533	
534	/-- The **schematic support** of a sheaf of modules `F` on a scheme `X`
535	(`def:schematic_support`): the closed subscheme of `X` cut out by the annihilator
536	ideal sheaf `annihilator F`. Project-local because `annihilator` is. -/
537	noncomputable def schematicSupport (F : X.Modules) : Scheme.{u} :=
538	  (annihilator F).subscheme
539	
540	/-- The canonical closed immersion of the schematic support into the ambient scheme,
541	realizing `schematicSupport F` as a closed subscheme of `X` (`def:schematic_support`).
542	This is the `IdealSheafData.subschemeι` of the annihilator ideal sheaf; it is a
543	`IsPreimmersion` + `QuasiCompact` immersion onto the support. Project-local because
544	`annihilator` is. -/
545	noncomputable def schematicSupportι (F : X.Modules) : schematicSupport F ⟶ X :=
546	  (annihilator F).subschemeι
547	
548	/-- The sheaf of modules `F` **has proper support over `S` along `f`**
549	(`def:has_proper_support`): the composite of the schematic-support immersion with

551	base change, this condition is preserved by pullback, as required by the Quot functor's
552	pullback action. Project-local because `schematicSupport` is. -/
